name: Micaiah the son of Imlah
charge: What the Lord saith unto me, that will I speak; against four hundred prophets and two kings
summary: Two kings sat in their robes at the gate of Samaria and four hundred prophets told them to go up and prosper. Jehoshaphat asked whether there was not one more. There was one, whom Ahab hated because he never prophesied good. The messenger who fetched him coached him to agree. He said he would speak what the Lord said, told them the truth, was struck on the face and sent to prison on bread and water until the king came back in peace. The king did not come back.
offense: Four hundred prophets encouraged the expedition to Ramoth-gilead, and the messenger sent for Micaiah urged him to agree. His answer was settled before he entered the court: what the Lord said, he would speak (1 Kings 22:6, 13-14). Agreement with a multitude was not his commission. Before the enthroned kings he declared that Israel would be scattered like sheep without a shepherd. He also disclosed the vision of the lying spirit sent to persuade Ahab through his prophets (1 Kings 22:17-23). The warning reached the king before the battle. Ahab was not left without testimony against the pleasant answer he preferred.
